name: Tailgating & Piggybacking
description: Tailgating is following an authorized person through a secured door without presenting credentials. Piggybacking is the same act with the target's knowledge — they hold the door for you. Both exploit social norms around courtesy and the assumption that someone moving confidently belongs there. Effective tailgating requires timing the approach as a valid user presents credentials, an appropriate cover story if challenged, and props that justify presence. Carrying large or awkward items dramatically increases success rates.

blue.det: Tailgating detection cameras; mantrap alert on multiple entries per badge read; security staff observing two people enter on one badge swipe; access log anomaly.
blue.cm: Mantrap or airlock vestibule enforcing one-person-at-a-time entry; tailgating detection cameras with real-time alerts; security awareness training empowering employees to challenge.
